design_doc_refutations: R1 (changes M2): VL-9's 'if !ok { return nil }' at 7 sites is WRONG — it is 5. The two template-loop sites (emitter lines 221 and 341) already panic with converter-specific messages, tagged M-DX12 / M-CODEGEN-UNIFIED-SLICE. Confirmed first-party in generated runtime.go: 5 literal converters return nil (598/614/632/654/676), ConvertToOptionSlice (853) and ConvertToResultSlice (877) panic. Consequence: the quorum's fallback REMOVAL applies to 5 emitter sites, not 'both emitters'; and design-doc AC4 clause (b) ALREADY PASSES AT BASE — it is a regression pin, not fail-at-base evidence.

R2 (widens M3): an ArrayVal reaching a template-loop converter PANICS, it does not silently return nil. Measured: Array[UserADT] compiles to NewPlanMkPlan(ConvertToDirSlice(tmp2)) with func NewPlanMkPlan(v0 []*Dir). examples/runnable/array_adt.ail is exactly this shape and is covered by make verify-examples, so B7 becomes a first-class M3 gate, not the afterthought AC6 implies. The doc does not flag this path.

R3 (narrows M3, and corrects its edit-site list): converter selection funnels through ONE chokepoint, Generator.getSliceConversion(goType) at codegen.go:715, with exactly 4 non-test call sites — codegen_decl.go:324, codegen_expr_app.go:139, codegen_record.go:174, codegen_record.go:337. getSliceConversion("ArrayVal") returns "" automatically, so no per-call-site surgery is needed. Conversely the doc's 'exhaustive' edit-site list OMITS codegen_decl.go (function return coercion), a 5th array path.

R4 (widens M3): ArrayVal is a NAMED type and 5 non-test sites branch on strings.HasPrefix(goType, "[]") — adt.go:451, codegen_match_patterns.go:34, codegen_decl.go:323, codegen_record.go:171, codegen_record.go:401. "ArrayVal" fails all five. Unlisted in the doc. Smaller instance of exactly why option (A) was rejected.

R5 (constrains the M2 fixture): std/array.empty and std/array.append emit undefined Empty/Append — `go build` rc=1 on the generated package. --no-verify-go (which the differential harness passes) hides it. std/array exports 10 functions; codegen emits helpers for 8. Pre-existing defect; the binding rule is that fixtures must not call append or empty.

R6 (recorded, not fixed): toSlice (codegen_runtime_collections.go:8) carries the same silent `return nil`, in a helper the source calls 'core infrastructure used by 24+ runtime helpers', reached from internal/builtins/registry_codegen_json.go:67,150 and registry_codegen_effects.go:52,245,258. Out of scope (type checker blocks arrays) but the quorum's stated universal goal is NOT met by M2 alone.

Minor: internal/gen/golang/*_test.go has ZERO references to TArray or ast.ArrayType (control: codegen_datastructures_test.go is the only test file matching 'Array' at all). The array type mappers have no unit coverage today — M3 breaks no existing test, but also has no safety net and must build one first.
Minor: go build ./... fails on cmd/wasm ONLY. The doc is right; the controller brief's additional 'gen/main' is not reproduced.

The design doc's form ('non-nil, len 3') is TOO COARSE: a converter doing make([]int64, len(src)) and never filling it returns a non-nil length-3 slice of zeros and passes. Baseline: literal converter -> nil; template converter -> panic.
M2.5 (REGRESSION PIN): ConvertToInt64Slice(nil) returns nil WITHOUT panicking — proves the legitimate `v == nil` branch survived the edit.

features.description:
THE MILESTONE THAT CLOSES THE USER-VISIBLE DEFECT, and the one holding all the sprint's risk. Budgeted 2 days (doc says 1) because of R2 and R4. Measured repro at base, single probe covering BOTH boundaries: `type Box = MkBox(Array[int])` -> `return NewBoxMkBox(ConvertToInt64Slice(tmp5))`, and `type Holder = { items: Array[int] }` -> `return &Holder{Items: ConvertToInt64Slice(tmp3)}`; interpreted '#[1, 2, 3]
#[4, 5, 6]
' vs compiled '[1, 2, 3]
[4, 5, 6]
'. This extends VL-16, which measured only the ADT path. Tasks: (1) types.go:79 case *types.TArray -> GoType("ArrayVal"), leaving case *types.TList (line 72) untouched. (2) adt.go:382 case *ast.ArrayType -> "ArrayVal", leaving *ast.ListType (320, 364) untouched. (3) DECIDE the adtSliceTypes side-effect: adt.go:386-389 registers g.adtSliceTypes[baseType]=true for user-defined array element types, and that registration is what CAUSES the template loop to emit ConvertTo<T>Slice — removing it may delete a converter a list path still needs; keeping it emits a dead one. go vet will not tell you (unused funcs are legal in Go); measure via TestGoldenCompile plus a grep on generated output, and record the decision in the commit. (4) AUDIT all 5 HasPrefix(goType, "[]") sites per R4 — adt.go:451, codegen_match_patterns.go:34, codegen_decl.go:323, codegen_record.go:171, codegen_record.go:401; codegen_match_patterns.go:34 (isTypedSlice) and codegen_record.go:171 (M-DX15 empty-literal) are likeliest to bite. (5) DO NOT hand-edit the four converter call sites — per R3 they all read getSliceConversion(goType) at codegen.go:715, which returns "" for "ArrayVal" automatically; VERIFY that via generated output (M3.4), do not assume it. (6) New mapper unit tests, each with its LIST CONTROL in the same test.
